newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesians jailed for burning church in East Java.
newsitem.headline: Indonesians jailed for burning church in East Java.

text.p: The first trial of rioters in East Java who burnt 25 churches last October has ended with five men receiving between seven and 10 months in jail for burning a church near the town of Situbondo, a court official said on Thursday.

Hariyoso, clerk of the Situbondo State Court, told Reuters the five men were convicted on Wednesday of arson involving a church and other buildings in Panurukan, about seven km (four miles) from the centre of Situbondo.

He said Indra Suprapto, 34, was sentenced to 10 months in jail, while M. Junaidi, 22, Rasid, 21, and Ansori, 30, all received eight months. A fifth man, Didik Santoso, 27, received a seven-month sentence.
The charges carried a maximum penalty of 12 years.

Five people were burnt to death in a church in Situbondo, 160 km (100 miles) east of Indonesia's second city of Surabaya, during the riots in early October triggered after a Moslem crowd became unhappy with the progress of a court case involving alleged blasphemy by a Moslem.
The crowd destroyed Situbondo's courthouse before going on the rampage, attacking the 25 churches and one temple. The man was later jailed as a heretic.
The trial of the five was the first of a number of hearings for 53 of 54 people arrested for allegedly taking part in the riots. One man died in custody from a respiratory disease.
